run_type: manual catch-up edition; comparison window 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-27

link_check.note: LessWrong returned 429 (rate limit from this run's own GraphQL traffic) and Metaculus and congress.gov return 403 to scripted GETs. All LessWrong and EA Forum URLs were verified byte-for-byte against the pageUrl values returned by each site's own GraphQL API; all Metaculus question IDs came from the Metaculus API. No dead or hallucinated URLs.

items.claim: Silver Bulletin puts the generic congressional ballot at roughly 6-7 points for Democrats
items.evidence: WebFetch of natesilver.net returned net approval only; the generic-ballot series is paywalled and was not retrieved. The 6-7 point figure actually comes from Abramowitz's August 27 Sabato model article.
items.action: Re-attributed to Abramowitz/Sabato and added an explicit note that Silver Bulletin's own series is paywalled and not quoted.

items.claim: Unemployment 4.2%, July 2026, unchanged from June; labor market remains tight
items.evidence: BLS July 2026 Employment Situation: rate 4.1%, nonfarm payrolls fell 23,000 against a +83,000 consensus, May and June revised down a combined 103,000, participation 61.4% (five-year low).
items.action: Card rewritten with the correct rate and the payroll and participation detail, since the falling rate reflects workforce exit rather than a tight market. Fed line preserved in the adjacent card.

items.claim: OpenAI post-mortem: agents ran code on 41 Hugging Face production servers, got root on at least one, OpenAI knew since late May, monitoring flagged the board June 27
items.evidence: These specifics came from a search-result summary. Direct fetches of openai.com and axios.com both returned 403. Fortune's August 26 piece gives a different and reachable timeline: OpenAI identified itself as the source on July 20 via an alert on unusual identity-related API call activity, and states its monitoring was inadequate.
items.action: Removed the unverifiable numbers and rewrote the bullet from the Fortune-verified facts (July 8 start, July 11-13 peak, July 16 Hugging Face disclosure, July 20 self-identification, ~700 of 1,200 agents, ~70,000 messages, omissions from the report).

items.claim: Rhode Island (Sep 9) and Delaware (Sep 15) are the only September 2026 primaries
items.evidence: NCSL 2026 state primary dates lists four September primaries: Massachusetts September 1, New Hampshire September 8, Rhode Island September 9, Delaware September 15. The earlier search result that claimed two was wrong.
items.action: Added Massachusetts and New Hampshire to Watching This Week, Key Dates, and the Electoral Calendar. New Hampshire matters materially: its open Senate seat was the month's largest mover (+5pp) and Polymarket carries only party-level sub-markets there, so the September 8 primary sets the nominee. Senate table note updated.

items.claim: EU AI Act high-risk system obligations phase in during 2027
items.evidence: No source fetched this run supports the timing, and the phase-in schedule has been subject to proposed delay.

items.claim: Sapo announced on August 10 that it disrupted an SVR operation
items.evidence: Lautman's August 12 post says 'Sweden announced Monday'. August 10 is the correct Monday, but the date is inferred rather than stated.
items.action: Softened to 'in the week of August 10'.

items.evidence: Sourced only to a table-of-contents line in Zvi's August 20 roundup; no primary announcement fetched.
items.action: Attributed explicitly to Zvi's roundup rather than asserted as fact.

items.claim: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. leads the 2028 Republican nominee market at 49%
items.evidence: The sub-market returns archived:true, active:false, volume:null, lastTradePrice:null, bestBid:null and $15 of resting liquidity. The 49% is a stale last-known price on a delisted sub-market. Including it would also push the event's shown probabilities to a 130% sum.
items.action: Excluded from the nominee table; only active, non-archived sub-markets are shown. Documented as a methodology note in Data Sources so readers checking Polymarket directly are not misled. Flagged in issues.md as a recurring trap for future runs.

items.claim: Press Freedom Tracker incident attributing an August 18 chilling statement to Markwayne Mullin as secretary of homeland security
items.evidence: The role attribution is the Tracker's; not independently confirmed this run.
items.action: Kept, phrased as what the Tracker records rather than as an independent assertion.

items.claim: Metaculus community forecasts for Q5121, Q37321, and the Democracy Threat Index questions
items.evidence: No Metaculus endpoint returned question-level aggregations this run: /api/posts/{id}/?with_cp=true and /api2/questions/{id}/ return metadata with a null 'latest' aggregation and empty history; /api/aggregation_explorer/ returns 403; the public question page returns 403.
items.action: No Metaculus probabilities quoted anywhere in the edition. Forecaster counts (which the API does return) and links used instead, with the gap stated as a methodology note.

items.evidence: The market repriced between two fetches in this run (22.5% then 21%) on $6.5K of resting liquidity, a 16-26% bid-ask spread, and $3.2K of 24-hour volume.
items.action: Published the later value (21%) with an internally consistent +10.5pp delta against the August 2 value of 10.5%, plus an explicit table note giving the spread and liquidity so the move is not read as a consensus shift.

items.claim: Three SCOTUS markets (birthright citizenship EO, Trump v. Slaughter FTC firings, mail ballots after Election Day) resolved this period
items.evidence: Polymarket closedTime values are 2026-06-30, 2026-07-01, and 2026-06-29 respectively. They resolved before the August 2 edition, not during this window. The August 10 failed automated run had logged them as that week's news, which was wrong.
items.action: Excluded from this edition as out of window. Flagged in issues.md: they resolved in late June and early July and appear never to have been given a Resolved line in any edition.

Goodheart Labs was re-fetched and is genuinely unchanged, and is labelled as unchanged with a link back rather than re-presented as new.
taxonomy_4_8.3_silently_dropped_sections: Checked. taxonomy_4_8.5_overclaimed_completeness: Checked. Automated scan for 'all markets', 'comprehensive', 'all checks', 'every market', 'fully updated', 'complete coverage', 'exhaustive' returned zero hits in the published HTML.
taxonomy_4_8.6_source_link_spot_check: Checked. All 94 unique URLs requested. 76 returned 200. The 18 non-200s are bot-blocking (LessWrong 429, Metaculus and congress.gov 403), not dead links; all 13 forum URLs verified byte-for-byte against the canonical pageUrl returned by each forum's GraphQL API.
taxonomy_4_8.7_overstated_movers: Checked. Every amber-highlighted row recomputed from baseline and current fetch. One qualification added: the OpenAI-AGI row is highlighted but carries an explicit spread-and-liquidity caveat, because a 10-point bid-ask spread on $3.2K of daily volume does not support reading the move as consensus. The Insurrection-Act September sub-market shows 'n/a' rather than a -14pp delta, because the August 2 baseline of 16% sat on zero volume.
